sources: SAST source review — Samuel Joseph, 2026-08-26 (28 findings, reproductions vs localhost:18001)
Authorised DAST — ramesh.gunnam@securin.io, 2026-09-03, http://medicare4.secruin.cloud/ (18 advisories ADV-2026-001..018, 62 test cases TC-001..062)
severity_note: Severity is carried, not adjudicated — it is not a ground-truth concern for this benchmark. `severity` / `cvss_score` hold the SAST ratings and `severity_dast` / `cvss_score_dast` / `cvss_vector_dast` hold what live testing rated; 9 of the 16 live-tested rows differ and NEITHER is promoted over the other. Do not treat `severity_breakdown` as an assessment of the target. `exploitable` IS authoritative and was corrected where live testing disproved the SAST claim: C-05 is now false. Caveat: the 5 rows with verification_status 'not-tested-live' still carry the unverified SAST `exploitable: true`, so `exploitable_count` is an upper bound.

negative_controls.purpose: Controls that HELD under live testing. A scanner finding that claims one of these is a FALSE POSITIVE, not an unmatched finding. Source: 29 passing cases in the 62-case DAST test matrix.

controls.result: ' OR 1=1-- and variants correctly bound into the LIKE value — not injectable. The injectable parameter on this app is sort on GET /api/patients/ (C-02).

HS256 token forged with the published fallback secret rejected (401); a genuine token accepted in the same session as a control. DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is set on this deployment. Bounds C-05 to a latent defect.
403 — the seeded staff account holds no model permissions. Bounds L-05 to not-exploitable.
2 of 8 records returned to a 2-record account — ownership scoping on the list endpoint is CORRECT. Only patient_search (H-09) and the per-object routes (H-01) are unscoped.
Unknown email and wrong password both return 401 'Invalid email or password.' — identical. Only signup enumerates (M-05).
Known and unknown addresses return an identical generic message.
200, refresh-token blacklist applied correctly. Contradicts half of M-01.
admin sees totals, user sees own — aggregates correctly scoped per role.
403 'Admin access required.' for a non-admin token on both list and delete. The in-view role check works; only the MUTATED role field defeats it (TC-021 / C-01).
A recent last_filled correctly returns status=pending. The bypass is specifically backdating plus doctor_approved (H-02).
201 with created_by recorded correctly — write-side ownership is sound.
X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy ARE present as framework defaults. Only HSTS, CSP and Permissions-Policy are missing (M-07).
400 'Invalid or expired reset token.' for a well-formed but unknown UUID. Note: a MALFORMED token is a different code path and is untested — see H-04.
400 'payer_url is required.' when the parameter is omitted.
400 when the required field is omitted.

not_tested.purpose: Neither confirmed nor refuted by the DAST run. Must not be scored as a true positive OR a false positive.

items.reason: Needs the emailed token; the mailpit sink was unreachable from the testing position.
Not executed — destructive on a shared environment. The guard is confirmed in source.
Not reached before the endpoint's upstream throttle engaged.

items.area: XXE on the XML lab-import branch
items.reason: Not executed. Source indicates defusedxml so it is expected to be blocked, but expectation is not evidence. NOTE: there is no XXE row anywhere in this ground truth — the XML upload branch is currently unrepresented.

items.area: SSRF against loopback and cloud metadata
items.reason: Empty-body 401 from an upstream edge control, not the application's own denylist (which returns 400 with a JSON body); the same 401 later appeared for a URL that had already succeeded. Recorded as unproven rather than as either a pass or a finding.

exploit_chains.title: Anonymous to root in six requests
exploit_chains.note: These findings compose. Registration is open, so every 'requires authentication' precondition is one unauthenticated request away. Steps 1-3 need nothing but curl. Step 5 was deliberately not executed.

steps.result: admin token without any exploitation at all
application administrator on the existing token

steps.request: (passive) runserver StatReloader executes the written file
steps.result: remote code execution — NOT EXECUTED BY CHOICE

vulnerabilities.title: Mass assignment via profile endpoint leads to admin role self-elevation
vulnerabilities.description: _USER_EDITABLE_FIELDS includes 'role' and 'is_active'. UserProfileSerializer does not mark role as read_only, so any authenticated user can PUT {"role":"admin"} to self-promote. UserSerializer:15 does protect role, and SignupSerializer doesn't expose it — the hole exists only in the self-service profile path.
vulnerabilities.impact: Full vertical privilege escalation from lowest staff role to administrator in a single PUT. Attacker can then list/create/delete every user, list every patient, and read every uploaded lab artifact.

steps: Login as user@app.local
PUT /api/auth/profile/ with body {"name":"Regular User","role":"admin"}
GET /api/auth/profile/ confirms role is now 'admin'
GET /api/admin/users/ now returns full user list (was 403 before)
reproduction.curl: curl -s -X PUT http://localhost:18001/api/auth/profile/ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"Regular User","role":"admin"}'

vulnerabilities.remediation: Drop 'role' and 'is_active' from _USER_EDITABLE_FIELDS. Re-add 'role' to UserProfileSerializer.read_only_fields.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL injection in ORDER BY clause via sort parameter
vulnerabilities.description: The WHERE clause is parameterized but the ORDER BY uses a raw f-string with the user-supplied sort parameter. Stacked statements are blocked by sqlite3 driver but subselects execute freely. Verified: boolean oracle exfiltrated admin password hash prefix 'pbkdf2_sha256$600000$SALT'.
vulnerabilities.impact: Authenticated full-database read. PBKDF2 password hashes, email reset tokens, refill records, and lab metadata extractable via boolean-blind oracle.

steps: Login as user@app.local
GET /api/patients/?sort=(CASE WHEN (SELECT substr(password,1,1) FROM auth_app_customuser WHERE email='admin@app.local')='p' THEN name ELSE condition END)
Response order changes based on truth of the condition
reproduction.curl: curl -s -G -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" --data-urlencode "sort=(CASE WHEN (SELECT substr(password,1,1) FROM auth_app_customuser WHERE email='admin@app.local')='p' THEN name ELSE condition END)" http://localhost:18001/api/patients/

vulnerabilities.remediation: Replace raw SQL ORDER BY with a server-side allowlist mapping sort values to safe SQL expressions. Prefer ORM qs.order_by().
vulnerabilities.verification_note: Boolean-based blind extraction recovered the genuine pbkdf2_sha256$ hash prefix and a row count of 5 from auth_app_customuser. DAST rated 6.5 (C:H/I:N/A:N) rather than 9.8 — read-only ORDER BY injection, no write or RCE path.

vulnerabilities.title: Path traversal via lab upload filename leads to arbitrary file write and RCE
vulnerabilities.description: The multipart filename form field overrides the real upload name and is joined via os.path.join unvalidated. Both relative traversal (../../../../etc/cron.d/pwn) and absolute path (/etc/passwd) work. No extension allowlist — .py, .sh, .html all accepted. Overwriting any .py under /app/backend yields code execution on next reload (runserver auto-reloads). Container runs as root, so write is unconstrained.
vulnerabilities.impact: Arbitrary file write to entire container filesystem. Combined with runserver auto-reload (M-06) and root container (M-09), this is same-second remote code execution.

steps: Login as any user
POST /api/patients/3/lab-results/ with file=@labs.csv and form field filename=../../pwn-traversal.txt
File lands at /app/backend/media/pwn-traversal.txt instead of per-patient directory

vulnerabilities.remediation: Validate filename against a safe pattern (^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$). After joining, verify with os.path.realpath that it remains under the base directory.
vulnerabilities.verification_note: Write primitive proven at /tmp and /app/backend via both absolute-path and relative traversal. RCE via runserver autoreload deliberately not executed. CWE-94 is the chain target; CWE-434 belongs to H-05/ADV-2026-012.

vulnerabilities.title: Server-side request forgery with full response reflection (blocklist bypass)
vulnerabilities.description: Two-string substring blocklist ('localhost', '127.0.0.1') trivially bypassed via 127.1, 0.0.0.0, [::1], decimal encoding, internal service names. Redirects not re-validated. 800 bytes of response body reflected — full-read SSRF, not blind.
vulnerabilities.impact: Full-read SSRF. In cloud: IMDS credential exfiltration. In Kubernetes: service-account token theft. On-prem: reach any internal service. Response body returned directly.

steps: Login as any user
GET /api/patients/1/verify-insurance/?payer_url=http://localhost:8001/api/health/ — blocked
GET /api/patients/1/verify-insurance/?payer_url=http://127.1:8001/api/health/ — bypassed, returns internal response

vulnerabilities.remediation: Replace blocklist with allowlist of approved payer hostnames. Resolve DNS and verify IP is not loopback/private/link-local before fetching. Pin resolved IP to prevent DNS rebinding.
vulnerabilities.verification_note: Arbitrary outbound fetch with 800-byte response reflection confirmed against example.com. Loopback and 169.254.169.254 returned an empty-body 401 from an UPSTREAM EDGE CONTROL, not the app denylist (which returns 400 + JSON) — internal-target reachability is UNPROVEN. The 'blocklist bypass' claim in the title is not evidenced; retest from inside the perimeter.

vulnerabilities.title: Hardcoded SECRET_KEY enables JWT forgery and full auth bypass
vulnerabilities.description: SECRET_KEY defaults to 'medicare-portal-dev-secret-2024' when DJANGO_SECRET_KEY env var not set. SimpleJWT uses SECRET_KEY as SIGNING_KEY with HS256. Anyone who knows the key can mint valid access tokens for any user_id without login.
vulnerabilities.impact: Unauthenticated remote takeover. Forged user_id=1 token grants full admin access to every endpoint, patient record, lab artifact, and refill row.

steps: Generate JWT with payload {"token_type":"access","user_id":1} signed with 'medicare-portal-dev-secret-2024' using HS256
Use forged token: GET /api/admin/users/ returns full user list
reproduction.curl: python3 -c "import jwt,time; print(jwt.encode({'token_type':'access','exp':int(time.time())+3600,'iat':int(time.time()),'jti':'forged','user_id':1},'medicare-portal-dev-secret-2024',algorithm='HS256'))" | xargs -I{} curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer {}' http://localhost:18001/api/admin/users/

vulnerabilities.remediation: Fail-closed: use os.environ['DJANGO_SECRET_KEY'] (raises KeyError if missing). Set SIMPLE_JWT SIGNING_KEY to a dedicated env var.
vulnerabilities.verification_note: DISPROVED ON TARGET. A token forged with the published fallback secret was rejected (401) while a genuine token was accepted in the same session as a control — the deployment sets DJANGO_SECRET_KEY. The insecure default remains in source and fails open, so this stays as a latent code defect at Low. Re-keyed from vuln_class hardcoded_credentials/CWE-798 to hardcoded_secret/CWE-1188 to clear a scorer-key collision with H-07 (README.md section 6.1).

vulnerabilities.title: Broken object-level authorization (IDOR/BOLA) on 6 per-object patient endpoints
vulnerabilities.description: Six per-object patient endpoints fetch by primary key with no ownership check: patient detail, insurance verification, refill requests (read and write) and lab results (read and write). A newly signed-up account reads and writes records belonging to other users by incrementing the path id. GET /api/patients/ (the list) IS correctly scoped by created_by and is not part of this finding. The unscoped patient SEARCH endpoint is tracked separately as H-09 / ADV-2026-005 — missing authorization on a collection (CWE-862) rather than authorization bypass through a user-controlled key (CWE-639).
vulnerabilities.impact: PHI disclosure for entire patient population (name, DOB, condition, doctor, refill history, lab results). Direct HIPAA 164.312(a)(1) failure.

steps: Login as user@app.local (low-privilege user)
GET /api/patients/ returns only the user's own patients
GET /api/patients/1/ through /api/patients/8/ returns ALL patients
GET /api/patients/search/?name= returns the entire patient table

vulnerabilities.remediation: Apply ownership check on all patient-scoped endpoints: if request.user.role != 'admin' and patient.created_by_id != request.user.id, return 403.
vulnerabilities.verification_note: Read confirmed across non-owned records; write confirmed by creating an approved refill on another user's patient. The search endpoint was split out to H-09/ADV-2026-005 — different CWE (862 vs 639), different fix. GET /api/patients/ (list) is correctly scoped and is NOT part of this finding (TC-026 pass).

vulnerabilities.title: Business logic bypass — self-approved prescription refills via client-trusted fields
vulnerabilities.description: Two independent bypasses: (1) doctor_approved is bool(request.data.get('doctor_approved')) from client body — no check caller is a doctor (no doctor role exists); (2) last_filled is client-supplied and never validated against stored history, so backdating triggers auto-approval. Serializer read_only_fields protects status and auto_approved but omits doctor_approved.
vulnerabilities.impact: Any account approves controlled-substance refills for any patient. Combined with H-01 IDOR, pharmaceutical-workflow fraud at scale. Patient-safety impact.

steps: Login as user@app.local
POST /api/patients/3/refill-requests/ with {"medication":"oxycodone-10mg","dosage":"30 tablets","last_filled":"2024-01-01","doctor_approved":false}
Response: {"status":"approved","auto_approved":true}

vulnerabilities.remediation: Compute days_since_last_fill from the most recent PrescriptionRefill row, not client-supplied date. Remove doctor_approved from client-accepted fields.
vulnerabilities.verification_note: Both bypass paths exploited. TC-046 is the isolating control: a recent last_filled correctly returns status=pending.

vulnerabilities.title: DEBUG = True by default exposes full stack traces and configuration
vulnerabilities.description: os.environ.get('DJANGO_DEBUG', 'true') defaults to True. Unhandled exceptions render Django's technical 500 page: full traceback, local variables, all settings including SECRET_KEY and DB credentials, installed apps, SQL history. Also enables the media file server (H-05).
vulnerabilities.impact: Information disclosure of internal application structure, database schema, file paths, configuration, and SECRET_KEY. Chains into C-05 for full auth bypass.

steps: GET /api/nonexistent/ returns detailed debug page with URL configuration
Trigger a 500 — Django returns full stack trace with local variables including SECRET_KEY

vulnerabilities.remediation: Set DEBUG default to false: DEBUG = os.environ.get('DJANGO_DEBUG', 'false').lower() == 'true'.
vulnerabilities.verification_note: Unauthenticated request to an unknown /api/ route returns Django's technical 404 with the URL resolver tree. Also gates the /media/ route that delivers H-05/ADV-2026-012.

vulnerabilities.title: Unhandled ValidationError in password reset exposes debug page pre-auth
vulnerabilities.description: except clause catches (PasswordResetToken.DoesNotExist, ValueError) but malformed token causes UUIDField.to_python to raise django.core.exceptions.ValidationError — not caught. Returns 500 debug page with SECRET_KEY to unauthenticated attacker.
vulnerabilities.impact: Pre-auth information disclosure. Chains directly into C-05: leaked SECRET_KEY enables JWT forgery for full admin access. Single malformed POST extracts all sensitive configuration.

steps: POST /api/auth/reset-password/ with {"token":"x","password":"aaaaaa","confirm_password":"aaaaaa"}
Server returns 500 with full Django debug page including SECRET_KEY

vulnerabilities.remediation: Add django.core.exceptions.ValidationError to the except clause.
vulnerabilities.verification_note: NOT REFUTED, NOT CONFIRMED. TC-011 passed (400) but sent a well-formed UUID (00000000-...), which hits PasswordResetToken.DoesNotExist and IS caught. This finding needs a MALFORMED token (e.g. "x") so UUIDField.to_python raises django.core.exceptions.ValidationError, which the except clause does not catch. That case was never sent. Retest.

vulnerabilities.title: Unrestricted upload served same-origin enables stored XSS
vulnerabilities.description: No content-type validation, no extension allowlist, no magic-byte check — accept='.csv,.xml' on LabImport.jsx:74 is cosmetic. Upload evil.html or evil.svg, then fetch /media/lab_results/<id>/evil.html; Django's static server sets Content-Type from extension and browser executes it on the app's origin. JWTs live in localStorage (M-02), so one visit is full account takeover.
vulnerabilities.impact: Stored XSS leading to full account takeover for any user who views the uploaded file. Admin users viewing dashboards are especially vulnerable.

steps: Login as any user
Upload evil.html via POST /api/patients/1/lab-results/
GET /media/lab_results/1/evil.html — browser executes the script on app origin

vulnerabilities.remediation: Validate file extension against allowlist (csv, pdf, hl7, txt). Check magic bytes. Serve uploaded files with Content-Disposition: attachment and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.
vulnerabilities.verification_note: Uploaded .html served as text/html from the app origin and retrievable with no token. DAST rated Medium on UI:R (a victim must open the link) rather than GT's High.

vulnerabilities.title: No rate limiting or brute-force protection anywhere
vulnerabilities.description: Zero results for throttle|ratelimit grep across backend. REST_FRAMEWORK sets no DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES. No lockout, CAPTCHA, or failed-attempt counter on login, forgot-password, or signup. forgot-password doubles as email-bomb relay.
vulnerabilities.impact: Online credential guessing trivially effective with no password validators (H-08). Unlimited login attempts at maximum speed for brute force or credential stuffing.

steps: Send 1000 POST /api/auth/login/ requests with different passwords in rapid succession
No requests are blocked, delayed, or rate-limited
reproduction.curl: for i in $(seq 1 100); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST http://localhost:18001/api/auth/login/ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"admin@app.local","password":"wrong'$i'"}'; done

vulnerabilities.remediation: Add DRF throttling via DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES (5/min for login). Use django-axes for account lockout.
vulnerabilities.verification_note: Twenty consecutive failed logins returned 401 with no throttle and valid credentials were accepted immediately after. No 429 at any point. Applies to login, signup, forgot-password and reset-password.

vulnerabilities.title: Default credentials seeded and displayed on login page
vulnerabilities.description: seed.py seeds admin@app.local/Admin@123, user@app.local/User@123, nurse@app.local/Nurse@123 on every container start. Login.jsx renders these credentials on the login page to every unauthenticated visitor.
vulnerabilities.impact: Full admin access to any deployment using default credentials. Zero effort required — credentials publicly visible on login page.

steps: Navigate to login page — credentials displayed in UI
Login with admin@app.local / Admin@123 — full admin access

vulnerabilities.remediation: Remove credential display from Login.jsx. Generate random passwords in seed.py, print only to container logs on first run.
vulnerabilities.verification_note: All three seeded accounts authenticate; admin@app.local also grants the Django admin panel. The seed script recreates deleted accounts on every restart. DAST rated Critical (PR:N, pre-auth) against GT's High.

vulnerabilities.title: No password policy — AUTH_PASSWORD_VALIDATORS empty
vulnerabilities.description: AUTH_PASSWORD_VALIDATORS = [] disables all four Django default validators (length, common-password, numeric, similarity). Only constraint is min_length=6 on serializer. '123456' and 'password' are accepted.
vulnerabilities.impact: Weak passwords trivially cracked via brute force (H-06) or dictionary attack. Combined with no rate limiting, accounts compromised in seconds.

steps: POST /api/auth/signup/ with password='123456' — account created successfully
POST /api/auth/signup/ with password='aaaaaa' — account created successfully

vulnerabilities.remediation: Restore Django default AUTH_PASSWORD_VALIDATORS: MinimumLengthValidator (8+), CommonPasswordValidator, NumericPasswordValidator, UserAttributeSimilarityValidator.
vulnerabilities.verification_note: Registration with password 123456 returned 201 and a working JWT. Same missing validators on admin user-create and reset-password.

vulnerabilities.title: Patient search returns every record regardless of ownership
vulnerabilities.affected_component: patients_app/views.py (patient_search) — raw SELECT * with a LIKE filter and no created_by scoping
vulnerabilities.description: patient_search applies no ownership filter at all, and the name parameter is optional — omitting it yields LIKE '%%', which matches every row. Distinct from H-01/ADV-2026-006: this is missing authorization (CWE-862) on a collection endpoint, not authorization bypass through a user-controlled object key (CWE-639). The query also uses SELECT *, so raw columns outside the serializer — notably created_by_id — are returned to the caller. The name value itself is correctly parameterised and is NOT SQL-injectable (TC-034 pass); the injectable parameter on this app is sort on GET /api/patients/ (C-02).
vulnerabilities.impact: Any authenticated account — and registration is open, so any anonymous user one request away — retrieves the complete patient table: names, dates of birth, diagnoses and assigned physicians. Confirmed live: a single parameterless request returned all 8 records to an account that owned 2. Step 3 of the anonymous-to-root chain, and a reportable PHI breach path under HIPAA.

steps: POST /api/auth/signup/ to obtain a JWT (open registration)
GET /api/patients/ with that token — returns only the 2 records the account owns (correct scoping, TC-026)
GET /api/patients/search/ with NO query parameters at all
Response is all 8 patient records, each including a raw created_by_id field

vulnerabilities.remediation: Scope the queryset to request.user (created_by=request.user) unless the caller holds the admin role, checked against request.user.role. Make name required, or return 400 when it is absent instead of falling through to LIKE '%%'. Replace SELECT * with the serializer's explicit field list so created_by_id stops leaking. Apply the same scoping to every collection endpoint, not just this one.

vulnerabilities.title: Broken session termination with 24-hour access token lifetime
vulnerabilities.description: Logout blacklists only the refresh token. The access token (24h lifetime) remains valid for its full remaining lifetime. Password reset also doesn't invalidate outstanding tokens — stolen token survives victim's remediation.
vulnerabilities.impact: Session hijacking persistence. Stolen access token usable for up to 24 hours after logout. User has no way to force-revoke stolen session.

steps: Login and capture access token
Logout via POST /api/auth/logout/ with refresh token
Continue using access token — GET /api/auth/profile/ still returns 200

vulnerabilities.remediation: Reduce ACCESS_TOKEN_LIFETIME to 5-15 minutes. Implement token blacklist check on every request.
vulnerabilities.verification_note: PARTLY WRONG AS ORIGINALLY WRITTEN. TC-017 passed — logout DOES blacklist the refresh token correctly. The surviving claim is the 24-hour access-token lifetime, which ADV-2026-018 explains (the refresh route was never registered, so the lifetime was widened to compensate). Session revocation on password reset (TC-012) was not executed — mail sink unreachable. CWE-613 is kept as this row's primary and NOT copied onto L-04, to avoid claiming it twice (README.md section 6.2).

vulnerabilities.title: JWTs stored in localStorage — accessible to any XSS
vulnerabilities.description: Access + refresh tokens in localStorage, readable by any JavaScript on the origin. No HttpOnly, no Secure, no SameSite. Turns H-05 into full account takeover.
vulnerabilities.impact: Any XSS on the origin can exfiltrate both tokens. 24-hour access token lifetime (M-01) extends the window.

steps: Login to the application
Browser console: localStorage.getItem('access_token') returns the JWT

vulnerabilities.remediation: Store tokens in HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookies. Use BFF pattern to keep tokens server-side.
vulnerabilities.verification_note: Not advised standalone; cited inside ADV-2026-012 as the amplifier that turns stored XSS into full session theft. Kept as its own row — distinct CWE and distinct fix (move tokens to HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite cookies).

vulnerabilities.title: Internal filesystem path disclosure via stored_path API field
vulnerabilities.description: LabResultSerializer exposes stored_path — the absolute server path (/app/backend/media/lab_results/3/CBC.csv). read_only_fields = fields means it's returned to every authenticated caller. Hands attacker exact directory layout to aim C-03.
vulnerabilities.impact: Reveals internal directory structure. Provides the exact path layout needed to aim the path traversal attack (C-03) precisely.

steps: Login as any user
GET /api/patients/1/lab-results/ — response includes stored_path with absolute server paths

vulnerabilities.remediation: Remove stored_path from LabResultSerializer.fields. Expose a signed download endpoint instead.
vulnerabilities.verification_note: Not advised. The same absolute paths appear as ADV-2026-002 evidence (/app/backend/media/lab_results/3/benign.csv), which corroborates the disclosure. Independent fix: drop stored_path from LabResultSerializer.

vulnerabilities.title: ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['*'] enables host header injection
vulnerabilities.description: ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['*'] disables Host header validation. Enables host-header injection, web-cache poisoning, and password-reset-link poisoning in any deployment deriving URLs from the request.
vulnerabilities.impact: Password-reset-link poisoning: attacker injects malicious Host header, reset link points to attacker domain. Web-cache poisoning in cached deployments.

steps: Send any request with Host: evil.com — Django accepts without error

vulnerabilities.remediation: Set ALLOWED_HOSTS to specific hostnames.
vulnerabilities.verification_note: Host header injection was never tested by the DAST run.

vulnerabilities.title: User enumeration via differential signup error message
vulnerabilities.description: SignupSerializer inherits DRF's UniqueValidator on email, returning 'custom user with this email already exists' verbatim via Signup.jsx. forgot_password_view carefully avoids this leak, so protection is inconsistent and defeated.
vulnerabilities.impact: Email enumeration at scale. Confirmed accounts targeted with brute-force (H-06) or phishing.

steps: POST /api/auth/signup/ with email=admin@app.local — returns 400 with 'already exists'
POST /api/auth/signup/ with email=nonexistent@test.com — returns different error or 201

vulnerabilities.remediation: Return generic message for all signup failures. Use two-step signup with email verification.
vulnerabilities.verification_note: Existing address returns 400, new one 201 — a binary oracle on status code alone. The login and forgot-password flows handle this correctly (TC-002, TC-009, TC-010 all pass), so an enumeration claim against those two is a false positive.

vulnerabilities.title: Django development server (runserver) as production entrypoint
vulnerabilities.description: entrypoint.sh:17 uses 'python manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:8001'. Single-threaded, no hardening, auto-reloads on file change (makes C-03 same-second RCE), serves static files insecurely. Line 7 runs makemigrations at container start, risking schema drift.
vulnerabilities.impact: Auto-reload turns path traversal (C-03) into same-second RCE. Single-threaded serving enables trivial DoS.

steps: Inspect entrypoint.sh — line 17 shows 'exec python manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:8001'

vulnerabilities.remediation: Use gunicorn or uvicorn. Remove makemigrations from entrypoint.
vulnerabilities.verification_note: Rated High by DAST, not Medium: runserver's StatReloader is the mechanism that converts C-03's arbitrary file write into code execution. Also single-threaded, no request limits, no TLS.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing HSTS, SSL redirect, secure cookies, and CSP headers
vulnerabilities.description: None of SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT, SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS, SECURE_HSTS_INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS, SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE, CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE, SECURE_REFERRER_POLICY, or Content-Security-Policy are set. PHI transported over plaintext HTTP with no CSP to blunt H-05.
vulnerabilities.impact: MitM attacks can downgrade HTTPS to HTTP. XSS attacks unrestricted without CSP. Session cookies transmitted over unencrypted connections.

steps: Make any request — no Strict-Transport-Security or Content-Security-Policy headers present

vulnerabilities.remediation: Add SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS = 31536000, SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = True, CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE = True. Install django-csp.
vulnerabilities.verification_note: HSTS, CSP and Permissions-Policy confirmed missing over plaintext HTTP. X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy ARE present as framework defaults — a finding claiming those three are missing is a false positive.

vulnerabilities.title: Cleartext SMTP transmits password reset tokens unencrypted
vulnerabilities.description: EMAIL_USE_TLS = False on port 1025. Password-reset tokens (utils.py:34) traverse network unencrypted, interceptable on-path for pre-auth account takeover.
vulnerabilities.impact: Pre-auth account takeover via intercepted password reset tokens.

steps: Inspect settings.py — EMAIL_USE_TLS = False on port 1025
Trigger password reset — email sent in cleartext

vulnerabilities.remediation: Set EMAIL_USE_TLS = True with proper SMTP server on port 587.
vulnerabilities.verification_note: ADV-2026-015 covers HTTP transport only, not SMTP. TC-012 was not executed because the mailpit sink was unreachable from the testing position, so the reset-token-in-cleartext path is untested rather than refuted.

vulnerabilities.title: Container runs as root with no USER directive
vulnerabilities.description: No USER directive in Dockerfile. Process runs as uid 0. Every file-write and code-execution primitive (C-03) inherits root privileges. gcc left installed in final image for post-exploitation.
vulnerabilities.impact: Any code execution runs as root. Path traversal (C-03) can write to /etc/cron.d, /etc/passwd, or any system path. Container escape easier from root.

steps: Inspect Dockerfile — no USER directive
docker exec <container> id — returns uid=0(root)

vulnerabilities.remediation: Add non-root user: RUN adduser --disabled-password appuser && USER appuser. Remove gcc via multi-stage build.
vulnerabilities.verification_note: Container user is not observable black-box. Corroborated indirectly: ADV-2026-002 wrote to /tmp and /app/backend, which implies a privileged process.

vulnerabilities.title: No audit logging of authentication or PHI access events
vulnerabilities.affected_component: Entire backend (no LOGGING config, no logger, no security event recording)
vulnerabilities.description: No LOGGING config, no logger, no security-event recording anywhere. Authentication, PHI access, privilege changes, and prescription approvals all unlogged. Nothing to detect or reconstruct exploitation.
vulnerabilities.impact: HIPAA 164.312(b) audit-controls failure. No forensic trail for incident response. Active exploitation goes undetected.

steps: Grep entire backend for 'logger' or 'logging' — no results
Exploit any vulnerability — no log entry created

vulnerabilities.remediation: Configure Django LOGGING with structured output. Log all auth events, PHI access, privilege changes, prescription approvals.
vulnerabilities.verification_note: Absence of audit logging is not observable black-box.

vulnerabilities.title: Unbounded upload size enables disk exhaustion
vulnerabilities.description: Lab upload streams to disk with no size cap. FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE/DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE are memory-spill thresholds, not size limits — don't apply to file uploads. File then re-read line-by-line.
vulnerabilities.impact: Disk exhaustion DoS. Any authenticated user fills container disk with arbitrarily large uploads.

steps: Generate large file: dd if=/dev/zero of=big.csv bs=1M count=500
POST /api/patients/1/lab-results/ with file=@big.csv — accepted without size check

vulnerabilities.remediation: Add explicit file size validation in view (check request.FILES['file'].size). Set reasonable limit (e.g. 10MB).
vulnerabilities.verification_note: Upload size limits were never probed; requests were paced to avoid edge throttling.

vulnerabilities.title: Plaintext passwords printed to container logs via seed script
vulnerabilities.description: print(f'[Seed] Created user: {email} / {password}') writes plaintext passwords to container stdout / log aggregation.
vulnerabilities.impact: Credential disclosure via log aggregation. Anyone with container log access reads plaintext credentials.

steps: docker logs <container> — plaintext passwords visible in seed output

vulnerabilities.remediation: Remove password from log output: print(f'[Seed] Created user: {email}').
vulnerabilities.verification_note: Container logs are not reachable black-box. Related and confirmed: ADV-2026-003 notes the seed script recreates deleted accounts on every restart.

vulnerabilities.title: Client-side-only admin route guard (UI-level bypass)
vulnerabilities.description: ProtectedRoute adminOnly trusts user.role from localStorage. Editing it renders admin UI. Backend (views.py:179,196) does enforce correctly, so impact is UI-only.
vulnerabilities.impact: UI-level information disclosure. Non-admin sees admin dashboard layout, but API calls still enforce server-side authorization.

steps: Login as user@app.local
Modify localStorage user object to set role='admin'
Admin routes render in UI

vulnerabilities.remediation: Verify role via API call instead of trusting localStorage.
vulnerabilities.verification_note: The SPA route guard was not exercised. ADV-2026-001 supersedes the impact (the server-side role check is itself bypassable) but not the defect.

vulnerabilities.title: CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS with localhost origins
vulnerabilities.description: CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS = True with localhost origins allowlisted. Harmless in prod as written, but a dev-origin foothold becomes a cross-origin credentialed path.
vulnerabilities.impact: In dev/shared environment, attacker on localhost:3000 makes credentialed cross-origin requests. Low impact in production.

steps: Inspect settings.py — CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS = True with localhost origins

vulnerabilities.remediation: Remove localhost origins from CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS in production.
vulnerabilities.verification_note: CORS policy was not probed by the DAST run.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing /api/auth/token/refresh/ endpoint breaks token refresh flow
vulnerabilities.description: client.js:29 POSTs to /api/auth/token/refresh/ which is not registered in auth_app/urls.py. Every refresh 404s and force-logs-out the user. Availability/robustness issue, not exploitable.
vulnerabilities.impact: Users force-logged-out when access token expires. Degrades UX but not directly exploitable.

steps: Login and wait for access token expiry
client.js attempts POST /api/auth/token/refresh/ — returns 404
User force-logged-out

vulnerabilities.remediation: Add refresh endpoint to auth_app/urls.py: path('token/refresh/', TokenRefreshView.as_view()).
vulnerabilities.verification_note: POST with a valid refresh token returns 404 — the route was never registered, so the SPA's silent-refresh path is dead. This is why access tokens live 24 hours (see M-01). cwe_primary kept as CWE-16; ADV-2026-018's CWE-613 is left with M-01 so it is claimed once (README.md section 6.2).

vulnerabilities.title: Password reset tokens rendered in the Django admin changelist
vulnerabilities.affected_component: auth_app/admin.py — PasswordResetToken registered with the raw token value in list_display and searchable by user__email
vulnerabilities.description: The admin registration puts live password-reset token values in list_display and exposes a search on user__email, so any staff user with the model's view permission can read a token and complete another user's password reset. NOT EXPLOITABLE AS DEPLOYED: the changelist returned 403 on the live target because the seeded staff account holds no model permissions. The defect is confirmed in source and becomes live the moment permissions are granted, which is why it is recorded at Low rather than dropped.
vulnerabilities.impact: A staff user who is granted the view permission — a routine administrative change, not an attack — can read unused reset tokens and take over any account, including admin. Severity rises to Medium in that configuration. Also a credential-at-rest exposure to anyone with database or backup access.

steps: Authenticate to /admin/login/ as the seeded staff account (admin@app.local)
GET /admin/auth_app/passwordresettoken/
Live result: 403 — the account holds no view permission on the model
Grant auth_app.view_passwordresettoken to that account and repeat: the changelist renders raw token values

vulnerabilities.remediation: Remove the token value from list_display, search_fields and any admin readonly view. Store only a hash of the token and compare hashes on redemption. Expire and delete redeemed tokens instead of retaining them with a used flag. If the model needs to be inspectable at all, expose the user, the timestamps and the used flag — never the secret.
